Discharge Summary:

Patient Name: [REDACTED]
Age: 58 years
Gender: Male
Date of Admission: June 8, 2020
Date of Discharge: [REDACTED]

Reason for Admission:
The patient was admitted on June 8, 2020, due to increased oxygen requirements following a COVID-19 diagnosis.

Hospital Course:
The patient received high flow nasal cannula therapy on admission. However, on hospital day 6, mechanical ventilation (MV) was initiated due to respiratory distress, hypoxemia, and hypercapnia. Despite MV, the patient's respiratory failure continued to worsen. Therefore, venovenous extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VV-ECMO) was implemented on hospital day 11. Meropenem, levofloxacin, convalescent plasma therapy, and dexamethasone were administered during the treatment course.

Outcome:
The patient showed gradual improvement in lung compliance and chest radiography. Ultimately, VV-ECMO was discontinued on hospital day 38.

Follow-Up Care:
The patient will continue to receive follow-up care and monitoring as required for complete recovery.
Primary Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]Secondary Diagnoses: [diagnosis section withheld]
Co-Morbidities:
None

Procedures Performed:
MV and VV-ECMO were performed during hospitalization.

Medications Upon Discharge:
There were no medications prescribed at the time of discharge.

Recommendations:
The patient was advised to continue following a healthy lifestyle routine and receiving regular medical checkups.

text:
**Principal diagnosis code: U07.1 COVID-19, virus identified**

**Rationale**
- The patient was admitted with increased oxygen requirements after a COVID-19 diagnosis. The course was progressive respiratory failure with pneumonia-type lung involvement, treated with high flow oxygen, mechanical ventilation and VV-ECMO.
- In ICD-10-AM (Australian Coding Standards, ACS 0112 Coronavirus Disease 2019), U07.1 is assigned when COVID-19 is confirmed by testing or the clinician documents it. When the patient is admitted for COVID-19, it is sequenced as the principal diagnosis.
- Manifestations are coded as additional diagnoses, not as the principal diagnosis.

**Likely additional diagnosis codes**, which depend on the withheld diagnosis section:
- J12.82 Pneumonia due to coronavirus disease 2019, if viral pneumonia was documented. In ICD-10-AM this may instead be J12.8 with U07.1, depending on the edition. Check your edition's tabular list.
- J96.0x Acute respiratory failure, with hypoxia and hypercapnia documented. The exact code depends on the edition's classification of type 1 versus type 2 failure.
- J80 ARDS, if documented by the clinician.
- Procedure codes (ACHI) for mechanical ventilation (continuous ventilatory support, by hours) and ECMO (extracorporeal membrane oxygenation, 13709-00 in ACHI).

**Caveats**
- The diagnosis section was withheld, so this is inferred from the clinical narrative.
- Confirm against the ICD-10-AM/ACHI/ACS edition in use, as the U07 and J12.8 conventions have changed between editions (11th edition onward).
